HyperLaw Implementation Plan (Build Order)

This is the step-by-step build order for the simplified HyperLaw system.

The goal is to implement a structured Incident → Case → Tutor system with minimal complexity first, then expand intelligence later.

⸻

PHASE 1 — CORE DATA STRUCTURE (FOUNDATION)

1. Create Data Models

Define simple core objects:

Incident

* id
* title (optional auto-generated or user-defined)
* description (user input text)
* date_of_event
* location (city/state optional)
* category (employment, police, appeal, other)
* created_at

Case

* id
* title
* list_of_incidents[]
* created_at
* status (open / in progress / closed)

Reminder

* id
* case_id
* label
* due_date

⸻

PHASE 2 — INCIDENT CREATION FLOW (PRIMARY USER ENTRY)

2. Build “New Incident” Screen

This is the MAIN action in the app.

User inputs:

* “What happened?” (large text field)
* When did it happen?
* Where did it happen?
* Type of situation:
    * Employment
    * Police interaction
    * Court / appeal
    * Other

Optional:

* attach files (future feature placeholder)

3. Save Incident Logic

* Save to local database / backend
* Do NOT run AI processing yet
* Do NOT generate citations
* Do NOT auto-analyze

⸻

PHASE 3 — CASE CREATION SYSTEM

4. Convert Incident → Case

After saving an Incident:

Prompt user:

“Add this to an existing Case or create a new one?”

If new:

* create Case object
* attach incident to case

If existing:

* append incident to case

⸻

5. Case View Screen

Each case shows:

* Case title
* List of incidents (chronological)
* Simple timeline view (basic list is fine initially)
* “Add Incident” button

NO AI PROCESSING HERE YET

⸻

PHASE 4 — REMINDER SYSTEM (LIGHTWEIGHT)

6. Add Reminder Feature

Inside Case view:

Button:

“Add Deadline Reminder”

User inputs:

* label (e.g. “filing deadline”)
* date

Store in Reminder table.

7. Profile → Reminders Section

Show:

* upcoming deadlines
* linked case name
* edit/delete options

Optional notifications later.

⸻

PHASE 5 — TUTOR LAYER (READ-ONLY AI)

8. Tutor Screen (Case-Aware)

Tutor reads:

* selected Incident OR Case

Tutor behavior:

* explains what user described in simple language
* identifies missing information
* suggests what to look into next
* asks clarifying questions

IMPORTANT RULES:

* No automatic filings
* No generating legal documents
* No assumed legal conclusions

Tutor is strictly:

“explanatory + educational assistant”

⸻

PHASE 6 — TEMPLATE SUGGESTION SYSTEM (ASSISTED ONLY)

9. Add “Suggested Templates” Section (static first)

Inside Case view:

Show:

* Complaint template (general)
* Civil cover sheet (general reference)
* Appeal forms (if applicable category selected)

Each item:

* description
* link to official source (manual links only)

NO auto-filling documents yet.

⸻

PHASE 7 — AI ENHANCEMENT LAYER (LATER PHASE)

Only after system is stable:

* integrate Claude
* enhance Tutor reasoning
* improve categorization suggestions
* optionally summarize incidents

BUT:
AI must remain optional and non-destructive.

⸻

IMPORTANT PRODUCT RULES

1. No background AI processing

Everything must be user-triggered or screen-triggered.

2. No auto legal conclusions

System must never assert legal outcomes.

3. Keep data explicit and visible

User should always see:

* incident text
* case structure
* reminders
* tutor explanations separately

⸻

FINAL PRODUCT FLOW

User experience should feel like:

1. User describes what happened
2. System saves it as an Incident
3. Incident is grouped into a Case
4. User views structured timeline
5. Tutor helps them understand it
6. Reminders help them stay on track

⸻

CORE DESIGN INTENT

HyperLaw is NOT:

* an AI legal decision engine
* an auto filing system
* a citation generator

HyperLaw IS:

a structured incident-to-case organizer with optional AI explanation support
